correctness.rationale: Direct subtraction of star components and strict monotonicity of v-h sin v for h<1 forces every predecessor of a diagonal target to remain diagonal. Exact calculus shows scalar f_c has two folds and precisely three inverse branches in (-a_c,a_c); the outer branches stay outside the fold range. At target zero the central inverse chain stays fixed and two new outer ancestors appear per level, giving 2n+1. At any other target, central inverse magnitudes grow geometrically and leave the branching interval; summation of the cubic Taylor remainder produces K(t)=log(1/|t|)/log(1/(c-1))+O_c(1), and each central level adds two persistent branches. Source domain and all critical-value boundaries treated; numeric checks supplementary.

value.rationale: The Huygens-network paper identifies an optimal invertibility threshold but does not quantify what fails in inverse reconstruction. This result gives sharp n-dependent growth at a dynamically canonical sink, proves all higher-dimensional inverse branches stay diagonal, and exposes a logarithmic target-space boundary layer with explicit coefficient. The dimension-independent whole-fiber census distinguishes noninjectivity complexity from qualitative Lyapunov convergence, in a natural range immediately above the sharp graph threshold.
